excerpt: StarkWare builds zero-knowledge STARK proof technology behind Starknet, StarkEx, the Cairo language and the S-two prover. Founders, funding at an $8 billion valuation and alternatives.
content:
StarkWare is an Israeli company that builds cryptographic proof technology for blockchains. Its work rests on STARKs, a kind of zero-knowledge proof that lets one computer prove to another that a large batch of computation was done correctly, without the other having to redo it. That lets blockchains such as Ethereum process many more transactions cheaply, because only a short proof has to be checked on the main chain.

Its main products are Starknet, a public network that runs on top of Ethereum; StarkEx, a scaling engine used by individual applications; Cairo, a programming language for writing provable programs, with syntax inspired by Rust; and S-two, its newest prover. StarkWare made S-two open source in 2025, said it set speed records, and in November 2025 S-two replaced the older Stone prover on Starknet mainnet. Starknet has its own token, STRK, first distributed through an airdrop.

The company's co-founders are Eli Ben-Sasson, Uri Kolodny, Michael Riabzev and Alessandro Chiesa. CTech dates the founding to 2017, while StarkWare's media kit says 2018. Kolodny was the first chief executive; he stepped down in January 2024 for family health reasons, and Ben-Sasson, previously president, became CEO.

In May 2022 StarkWare raised $100 million in a Series D led by Greenoaks Capital and Coatue at an $8 billion valuation, four times the $2 billion of its Series C six months earlier, TechCrunch reported. CTech later reported that the company was cutting jobs and shifting from infrastructure and research toward revenue-generating products.

StarkWare does not sell a priced subscription. Developers use Starknet by paying network fees, and Cairo and S-two are open source.

This page is research, not a review: StarkWare has no product we could try. It brings together StarkWare's own website and the reporting linked under Sources, and says where each fact comes from.
